catalog.description: How to write decision records and project docs for an agent or teammate with no memory of the project's history — document the resulting state, not the change. Use whenever someone says "write an ADR" or "document this decision".
catalog.index: recording a decision or writing docs

catalog.description: Design standards for building CLI tools that agents drive through the shell — TOON output, minimal schemas, structured errors, ambient context. Use whenever you build, modify, or review an agent-facing CLI whose project declares AXI conformance.

How to write code comments — what earns a comment, what stays out, and the register they use. Use whenever writing or editing code that carries comments, docstrings, or doc comments, or when reviewing comment prose in a diff.

The delegation discipline — when to spawn a subagent, how to charge and scope it, when it needs an isolated worktree, and how a done-claim is verified. Use whenever you spawn any delegate or accept one's result. The line lives in craft-line.
catalog.index: spawning a delegate / verifying a delegate's done-claim

catalog.description: How to consume a project's design system when building UI. Use whenever building or modifying a UI component, applying a color/spacing/type/motion value, or composing a component.

The domain-modeling companion — canonical terms with Avoid lists, scenarios at concept edges, and code-versus-claim checks. Use during grilling, shaping, or spec authoring, or whenever a term feels vague, overloaded, or contradicted by the code.
catalog.index: pinning domain terms / enumerating concept-edge scenarios

catalog.description: How to author the oracle — add, edit, weaken, or remove a gate check, choose its fail posture, and prove it bites. Use whenever you touch .bench/gate.sh or any project gate, wire an enforcement hook, or scaffold a gate in /bench-setup-repo.
catalog.index: adding, weakening, or removing a gate check / authoring the oracle

catalog.description: Disciplined frontier-round elicitation to surface a decision or a spec — each numbered round asks every question whose prerequisites are settled. Use during /bench-shape-idea decision tickets, before /bench-write-spec, or when I say "grill me".
catalog.index: surfacing decisions in numbered frontier rounds

catalog.description: How to pick and govern the line — which model tier and effort a build, shift, TDD pass, or delegated task gets, and when a tier moves. Use whenever you declare the line (invariant 2), choose a model for a subagent, or escalate a tier.
catalog.index: declaring the line / picking a delegate's model or effort

catalog.description: The research discipline — the factual question graph, primary sources only, and one cited durable output per run. Use whenever the work becomes factual reading legwork in shaping, specification, diagnosis, assessment, or implementation.
catalog.index: doing factual reading legwork / writing a cited research report

catalog.description: The three-axis review judgment — Standards, Spec, Coverage — and the citation standard a finding must meet. Use whenever you review a diff: the /bench-review-implementation phase, a delegate's work, a PR, or a self-review. Advisory, never the oracle.
catalog.index: reviewing a diff / what a finding must cite

catalog.description: Vocabulary and principles for placing test seams and designing deep modules. Use whenever someone asks "where should this test live" or "is this the right boundary to test", or when /bench-write-spec picks seams — even on small changes.
catalog.index: placing a test / designing an interface

catalog.description: Principles for writing and editing skills so they fire reliably and stay lean. Use whenever creating, editing, reviewing, or pruning any skill — the kit's own skills or your project's.

The spec-authoring discipline — the acceptance-coverage-map row schema, how stories and scope cuts are sized, and how a build is sliced into review chunks. Use when you author or audit a spec, write coverage rows, or decide an edge is a Won't handle.
catalog.index: coverage-map rows, edge inventories, story sizing, and review-chunk slicing for a spec

catalog.description: The discipline for safely folding a candidate change into the Bench kit — respect closed decisions, assess by the gap it fills, pass the legibility, consistency, and dogfood loops, and propose rather than merge. Use when you evaluate a kit change.

catalog.description: How to apply test-driven development without the cost blowup or the over-fit-and-stop failure. Use whenever writing tests first, someone says "red-green-refactor" or "write the test first", or building at a seam that /bench-write-spec marked for TDD.

How to break a spec or small change into tracer-bullet tickets — complete vertical slices, demoable alone, one context window each — with blockers and review-chunk membership. Use during spec authoring, or when you decide what lands green next.

# `bench worktree create` advertises the label-addressed next action

Blocked by: none
Writes: internal/worktree/worktree.go, internal/worktree/*_test.go, .agents/skills/bench-craft-delegate/SKILL.md

## What to build

After the `worktree_create` table, `bench worktree create` prints a `next[2]:`
block. The block names the label-addressed verbs: `bench worktree exec "<label>" -- <command>`
and `bench worktree path "<label>"`. A caller never caches the path in a
scratch variable. The `bench-craft-delegate` skill's Isolation passage states
the same rule. A caller addresses a created worktree by label
through `bench worktree exec`/`path`, never through a cached `$WT`.

- [ ] `bench worktree create --request r --label "x"` output ends with a `next[2]:`
      block whose lines contain `bench worktree exec "x" -- <command>` and
      `bench worktree path "x"`; a test asserts it.
- [ ] Delegate skill Isolation passage carries the sentence.
- [ ] `bench gate` green.
